text: Code refactoring means improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. The program should behave exactly the same after refactoring, so users do not notice any difference. Developers refactor code to make it cleaner and easier to read. When code is well organized, it is simpler to find bugs and add new features. Refactoring also helps reduce technical debt, which builds up when quick fixes and poor design make code hard to maintain. Regular refactoring keeps a project healthy and saves time in the long run, even though it does not add new functionality.
